short: The Mamluks beat a Mongol army in open battle and fixed the limit of Mongol expansion west.
full:
After Möngke's death Hulagu withdrew east with the bulk of his army, leaving perhaps 10,000 men in Syria under the Naiman general Kitbuqa. His envoys reached Cairo demanding surrender; the Mamluk sultan Qutuz had them beheaded and their heads displayed on the Bab Zuweila gate, then marched north with an army that included Baibars, and secured a wary passage through Crusader Acre.

The armies met on 3 September 1260 at the spring of Ain Jalut in the Jezreel Valley. Baibars skirmished and fell back, drawing Kitbuqa into hills where Qutuz had hidden the main force, and the Mongols were enveloped. Kitbuqa was captured and killed. The Mamluks, themselves largely Kipchak Turks bought as slaves from the steppe the Mongols had emptied, fought in the same tradition and were not intimidated by it. Syria was recovered within weeks. Qutuz was murdered on the road home and Baibars took the throne. The Mongols raided Syria for decades but never held it.
